variations.name: Industrial slow-pyrolysis biochar plants
variations.description: Continuous industrial reactors bake forestry and agricultural residues without oxygen into stable biochar plus usable process heat/power, locking ~2-3 tCO2 per tonne of char for centuries while producing a saleable soil product; this route delivers the large majority of all durable carbon removal credits retired to date.

companies.name: Exomad Green
companies.what: Operates the world's largest biochar facilities in Bolivia (Concepcion, Guarayos), converting sawmill/forestry residues at industrial scale and giving char free to indigenous communities
companies.signal: ~260,000 tCO2/yr removal capacity; ~27% of all delivered durable CDR; Microsoft 1.24 Mt offtake (May 2025), the largest biochar deal ever

companies.name: NetZero
companies.what: Builds coffee-husk pyrolysis plants in tropical farming regions (Brazil, Cameroon) and sells char back to growers as fertilizer complement
companies.signal: €18M from STOA (Mar 2024) on top of €11M Series A (~$39M total); 4 commercial sites in Brazil; XPRIZE Carbon Removal finalist

companies.name: Novocarbo
companies.what: Develops 'Carbon Removal Parks' across Europe that co-locate pyrolysis with industrial customers buying the waste heat
companies.signal: €25M from SWEN Capital Partners (2024); roadmap of up to 200 parks across Europe

companies.name: Carbo Culture
companies.what: Patented pressurized 'carbolysis' reactors; its R2 plant in Honkajoki, Finland is one of Europe's largest single biochar units
companies.signal: ~$26M+ raised (True Ventures et al.); €3.5M Dutch grant to launch ARC Middenmeer plant in North Holland (announced Mar 2026)

companies.name: Oregon Biochar Solutions
companies.what: Runs one of the largest US biochar plants (White City, OR) on forestry waste, producing 24/7 at industrial volume
companies.signal: Puro.earth-certified CORC supplier; credits retailed via Climate Impact Partners

companies.name: Standard Biocarbon
companies.what: Continuous PYREG-based plant using sawmill residuals, co-located with Pleasant River Lumber in Maine
companies.signal: First-of-kind Maine facility (ReGenerate Livermore Falls) producing and Puro-certified since 2024

companies.name: Wakefield Biochar
companies.what: Produces biochar at three US sites partnered with pulp and sawmills and sells consumer/agricultural soil products at retail scale
companies.signal: Multi-site production per April 2025 industry mapping; one of the most distributed US brands

companies.name: Carbofex
companies.what: Early Finnish producer (since 2017) making biochar plus bio-oil from spruce chips, an early Puro.earth supplier
companies.signal: ~700 t char + 600 t bio-oil/yr; supplied credits to Microsoft and Shopify; Carbon XPRIZE Top-60

companies.name: Cool Planet Energy Systems
companies.what: Pyrolysis 'carbon-negative gasoline' plus Cool Terra engineered biochar; the sector's biggest venture failure and a cautionary tale on fuel-plus-char economics
companies.signal: Raised ~$235M from BP, Google Ventures, ConocoPhillips, NRG; wound down operations around 2020

variations.name: Gasification-route biochar with syngas/electricity co-generation
variations.description: Wood gasifiers partially convert biomass to syngas for combined heat and power and deliberately leave a carbon-rich char residue, so every kWh of dispatchable renewable power also yields certified carbon removal — economics lean on the energy sale rather than the char.

companies.name: Syncraft
companies.what: Austrian two-stage 'floating-bed' wood gasification power plants (200-500 kWel) producing electricity, district heat and certified biochar
companies.signal: >25 plants in continuous operation (Austria, Italy, Japan, Croatia) with 800,000+ cumulative operating hours; new plant opened May 2025

companies.name: Burkhardt Energy
companies.what: Series-manufactured wood-pellet gasifier CHP modules (V3.90 line) with char co-product, factory-built in Bavaria since 2010
companies.signal: Hundreds of CHP units deployed across Europe

companies.name: Spanner Re2
companies.what: Holz-Kraft containerized wood-chip gasifier CHPs for farms, hotels and district heat with biochar output
companies.signal: Several hundred plants installed worldwide; one of the longest-standing small-gasifier OEMs

companies.name: Rainbow Bee Eater
companies.what: Australian ECHO2 gasification units that pipe syngas heat into industry (e.g., glasshouses) while producing biochar from green waste
companies.signal: Operating units near Melbourne; credits purchased by Shopify and Microsoft

companies.name: All Power Labs
companies.what: Berkeley maker of container-scale downdraft gasifier gensets (PP30, Powertainer) producing distributed power plus biochar; new Gen3 'swirl hearth' reactor
companies.signal: Units shipped to 40+ countries over more than a decade

companies.name: CHAR Technologies
companies.what: Canadian high-temperature pyrolysis/gasification converting wood waste and digestate into renewable gas plus biocarbon (CleanFyre) for steelmakers
companies.signal: TSXV-listed (YES); Thorold, Ontario commercial facility

variations.name: Mobile and village-scale pyrolysis units
variations.description: Small transportable carbonizers, tractor-mounted units and trained smallholder kiln networks convert dispersed agricultural and forestry residues into biochar at the field edge, avoiding open burning and biomass haulage costs — the cheapest feedstock in the world, but the hardest to monitor.

companies.name: Takachar
companies.what: MIT spinout making low-cost, tractor-mountable units that convert crop residue to char/bioproducts in-field to stop residue burning
companies.signal: Earthshot Prize 2021 winner; Takavator Mini (~100 kg/hr) deployed in southern India, US West Coast and British Columbia

companies.name: Applied Carbon
companies.what: Self-propelled in-field pyrolyzer trailers (ex-Climate Robotics) that pick up crop residue, char it, quench it and spread it on the field in one pass
companies.signal: $21.5M Series A (Aug 2024) led by TO VC with Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund participation

companies.name: Biochar Life
companies.what: Trains smallholder farmers in Kenya, Malawi and Thailand to make artisanal biochar (Kon-Tiki/trench kilns) and aggregates C-Sink credits
companies.signal: Sells via Carbonfuture; deploying WasteX semi-automated carbonizers across its network from 2025

companies.name: WasteX
companies.what: Singapore/Indonesia startup selling small semi-automated carbonizers to rice and poultry mills with credit revenue sharing
companies.signal: $450k from P4G (2024); trials showing 38-95% yield gains with halved fertilizer in Philippines/Indonesia

companies.name: HUSK
companies.what: Cambodia/Vietnam venture turning rice husks into biochar-based fertilizers for smallholders, now adding a dedicated pyrolysis plant with atmosfair
companies.signal: Mekong Capital investee; Kampong Thom plant commissioned Nov 2025 (~3 t char/day from 6 t husks)

companies.name: Air Burners
companies.what: Florida maker of mobile air-curtain burners whose CharBoss model (developed with USDA Forest Service) converts forestry slash to char on-site
companies.signal: CharBoss units sold to utilities and forestry agencies for wildfire-fuel reduction

companies.name: Tigercat
companies.what: Canadian forestry-equipment manufacturer producing the 6050 Carbonator, a tracked mobile carbonizer for slash disposal
companies.signal: In serial production within an established global forestry equipment line

variations.name: Hydrothermal carbonization of wet wastes (hydrochar)
variations.description: Pressurized hot water (~180-250C) 'cooks' wet feedstocks like sewage sludge, manure and food waste into coal-like hydrochar without energy-intensive drying, solving a disposal problem and enabling phosphorus recovery — though hydrochar's lower carbon permanence limits its carbon-credit value versus pyrolysis char.

companies.name: TerraNova Energy
companies.what: German HTC technology (TerraNova Ultra) for sewage sludge with integrated phosphorus recovery; industrial reference plant in Jining, China
companies.signal: Operating industrial references in Germany and China; licenses to utilities

companies.name: Ingelia
companies.what: Spanish pioneer running continuous industrial HTC at Naquera since 2010 and licensing plants internationally
companies.signal: Longest-running industrial HTC plant; licensees including CPL in the UK

companies.name: C-Green
companies.what: Swedish OxyPower HTC modules that use wet oxidation to make sludge-to-hydrochar nearly energy self-sufficient
companies.signal: First commercial unit at Stora Enso's Heinola mill (Finland); further Nordic deployments

companies.name: HTCycle
companies.what: German sewage-sludge HTC plant at Relzow with phosphorus recovery as the revenue anchor
companies.signal: Consistently ranked among the top HTC players in 2025 market surveys

companies.name: CPL Industries
companies.what: UK smokeless-fuel incumbent operating an Ingelia-licensed HTC line (Immingham) to make waste-derived briquettes
companies.signal: Decades-old solid-fuels business; listed among leading HTC companies 2025

companies.name: AVA-CO2 (AVA Biochem)
companies.what: Built the world's first industrial-scale HTC plant (Karlsruhe, 2010) before exiting HTC to pivot to 5-HMF biochemicals
companies.signal: Early-mover cautionary tale: HTC business wound down in the mid-2010s for lack of offtake economics

variations.white_space: Hydrochar is less recalcitrant than pyrolysis char so registries award few or no durable-CDR credits, leaving plants to live off sludge tipping fees; EU bans on sludge landspreading and phosphorus-recovery mandates create a utility-partnered niche that remains thinly served — an opening for waste majors (Veolia/SUEZ-style) to roll up the licensors.

variations.name: Bio-oil and bio-slurry deep-well injection for permanent storage
variations.description: Biomass is converted to a pumpable carbon-rich liquid (fast-pyrolysis bio-oil) or slurry and injected into regulated deep disposal wells, where it solidifies for 1,000+ year storage — trading biochar's soil co-benefits for maximum permanence and verifiability.

companies.name: Charm Industrial
companies.what: The category creator: mobile fast pyrolyzers convert crop residue and wildfire-risk biomass into bio-oil injected into EPA-regulated disposal wells
companies.signal: $100M Series B (2023); $53M Frontier offtake, Google and JPMorgan purchases, TD Bank deal with Canada expansion (2025); tens of thousands of tonnes delivered

companies.name: Vaulted Deep
companies.what: Injects slurried organic wastes (biosolids, manure, paper sludge) into deep geologic formations using oilfield slurry-injection IP — same storage logic without the pyrolysis step
companies.signal: $32M Series A (Prelude); won $50M XPRIZE grand prize... ($8M category, Apr 2025); Microsoft 4.9 Mt 12-year deal (Jul 2025); CNBC Disruptor 50 (2026)

companies.name: MASH Makes
companies.what: Danish-Indian company whose containerized pyrolysis lines yield biochar plus carbon-negative bio-oil, proven as drop-in marine fuel and a candidate storage feedstock
companies.signal: Nefco financing; Karnataka plant processes ~23,700 t agri-waste/yr (~3,400 t bio-oil); world-first vessel trial on its biofuel; second plant tripling capacity

companies.name: Carba
companies.what: Minnesota startup using low-temperature pyrolysis (torrefaction) then burial of the carbon in engineered landfill-style pits — a low-cost storage cousin of injection
companies.signal: $7M DOE Carbon Negative Shot grant; Microsoft 44,000-credit 5-year deal; $6M round (Rusheen, CanopyGen) for US and Asia expansion

variations.white_space: Charm is still the only company injecting pyrolysis bio-oil at scale — bio-oil is corrosive, costs run several hundred dollars per tonne, and injection-well permitting is slow — so the opening is regional pyrolysis hubs feeding shared disposal wells and oilfield-services incumbents (who already drill and permit these wells) offering 'storage as a service' to any bio-oil producer.

variations.name: Biochar soil-application networks and credit aggregators/registries
variations.description: Registries, MRV platforms and project aggregators certify that char is actually produced, tracked and applied to soils or materials, turning fragmented biochar production into bankable carbon credits — the connective tissue that made biochar ~90% of delivered durable CDR.

companies.name: Puro.earth
companies.what: Nasdaq-majority-owned registry whose CORC standard underpins most industrial biochar credits worldwide
companies.signal: >400,000 biochar CORCs issued by mid-2025; biochar credit market grew >40% in volume in 2025

companies.name: Carbonfuture
companies.what: German digital MRV ('MRV+') and marketplace tracking char from kiln to end use; infrastructure behind the largest supplier programs
companies.signal: Tracks the Exomad-Microsoft 1.24 Mt deal and Swiss Re's 70,000 t biochar program

companies.name: Isometric
companies.what: Science-first CDR registry whose Biochar Production & Storage protocol was ICVCM-approved in 2025, used by quality-focused corporate buyers
companies.signal: $25M seed (Lowercarbon, Plural); biochar protocol live alongside Frontier-aligned buyers

companies.name: Varaha
companies.what: Indian developer aggregating smallholder and industrial biochar projects (incl. Gujarat facility) across South Asia
companies.signal: Google offtake of 100,000 t (Jan 2025) — world's largest biochar deal at signing; only Indian supplier listed on Puro.earth at the time

companies.name: Carbon Standards International
companies.what: Swiss certifier running the EBC (European Biochar Certificate) and Global C-Sink standards covering both industrial and artisanal char sinks
companies.signal: De-facto EU biochar quality standard; artisanal C-Sink methodology used across the Global South

companies.name: Pacific Biochar
companies.what: Retrofits idle California biomass power plants for char production and routes it through compost and farm soil-application networks
companies.signal: Early Microsoft biochar supplier (1,500 t CO2 in 2021); multiple California facilities

companies.name: Verra
companies.what: World's largest voluntary carbon registry; its VM0044 biochar methodology brings biochar into the mainstream VCM
companies.signal: VM0044 v1.2 ICVCM-approved in 2025 alongside Isometric and CAR biochar methodologies

variations.name: Biochar-embedded materials (concrete, asphalt, plastics, filtration media)
variations.description: Biochar is blended into concrete, asphalt, polymers and filtration media as a lightweight carbon-storing filler that can also cut cement content, turning buildings and roads into carbon sinks and stacking embodied-carbon savings on top of sellable removal credits.

companies.name: Bioforcetech
companies.what: Pyrolyzes wastewater biosolids into OurCarbon, used commercially in concrete, asphalt and inks
companies.signal: Commercial Bay Area concrete pours with Vulcan Materials' Central Concrete, SOM and Cahill (incl. an Oakland school, 2025)

companies.name: ecoLocked
companies.what: Berlin startup making biochar-based admixtures that replace part of the cement binder in ready-mix concrete
companies.signal: €4M seed (Matterwave, Climentum, 2023) on top of €1.8M pre-seed; pilots with concrete producers

companies.name: Glanris
companies.what: Memphis company converting rice hulls into patented biocarbon water-filtration media, with concrete and asphalt applications
companies.signal: Patented rice-hull media; certified carbon-removal claims; commercial filtration sales

companies.name: Made of Air
companies.what: German maker of HexChar, a biochar-filled thermoplastic for facades and retail interiors (used by Audi, H&M pilots)
companies.signal: Raised ~$5-6M (2022); little public activity since 2024 — commercial status unclear

companies.name: Verde Resources
companies.what: US-listed developer of BioAsphalt/BioFraction putting biochar into net-zero road construction, working with NCAT test tracks
companies.signal: Named by the International Biochar Initiative (2025) as the pioneer of biochar asphalt R&D and pilot roads

companies.name: Myno Carbon
companies.what: Washington-state producer building mill-co-located biochar plants and marketing char specifically for concrete and asphalt
companies.signal: First plant sited at a WA pulp mill; targets 5 Mt CO2/yr across facilities by 2030

variations.white_space: Construction codes and conservative mix-design specs make adoption slow, and biochar must beat near-free fillers like fly ash on cost; Made of Air's stall shows the product risk — the opening is code-approved, EPD-backed admixtures sold through ready-mix incumbents that stack embodied-carbon reductions with CDR credit revenue.

variations.name: Pyrolysis reactor OEMs and technology licensors
variations.description: Equipment makers and licensors supply the kilns, screws and carbonization modules every biochar project depends on, monetizing the boom through capex sales and royalties rather than carbon credits — the 'picks and shovels' of the sector.

companies.name: PYREG
companies.what: Leading German net-carbon-tech OEM (PX series) for biomass and sewage-sludge carbonization; the reactor behind many US/EU plants
companies.signal: ~60+ systems delivered worldwide; SUEZ partnership for Pyrolis S2B sludge-to-biochar (deployed early 2026); expansion financed by new shareholder Vaering

companies.name: Biomacon
companies.what: German maker of heat-led modular carbonization reactors sized for greenhouses and district heating
companies.signal: C500-I unit (~450 t char/yr) selected for flagship UK biochar projects

companies.name: Airex Energy
companies.what: Quebec OEM (CarbonFX torrefaction/pyrolysis) and co-owner of Carbonity, Canada's largest biochar plant at Port-Cartier
companies.signal: Series D raised (2024); Carbonity inaugurated May 2025 at 10,000 t/yr scaling to 30,000 t/yr; 350,000 t/yr roadmap with SUEZ by 2035

companies.name: Pyrocal
companies.what: Australian designer of CCT carbonization systems for councils and agro-processors, handling difficult feedstocks including biosolids and nut shells
companies.signal: Systems deployed across Australia and Asia; supplies technology to large credit-generating projects

companies.name: VOW ASA (ETIA/Biogreen)
companies.what: Oslo-listed group whose ETIA Biogreen/Spirajoule electrically heated screw pyrolysis is sold for biochar and biocarbon production lines
companies.signal: Listed company; Biogreen units installed globally across waste and biomass applications

companies.name: Beston Group
companies.what: Chinese equipment manufacturer mass-producing low-capex continuous carbonization/charcoal lines exported worldwide
companies.signal: High-volume export OEM serving 100+ countries at price points far below Western rivals

companies.name: Klean Industries
companies.what: Vancouver integrator of pyrolysis/carbonization plants (biomass, tires) bundled with carbon-credit project development
companies.signal: Projects and JVs across North America and Asia

variations.name: Fast-pyrolysis bio-oil production for fuels and chemicals
variations.description: Rapid high-temperature pyrolysis maximizes the liquid fraction, producing pyrolysis oil that is co-processed in refineries, burned as renewable heating fuel, or upgraded to chemicals — the industrial bio-oil base that the carbon-removal injection pathway now builds on.

companies.name: BTG Bioliquids
companies.what: Dutch licensor of rotating-cone fast pyrolysis; the technology behind the Empyro, Pyrocell and Green Fuel Nordic plants
companies.signal: 4+ commercial plants built on its technology; modular 500-bpd biorefinery JV with NanosTech (2024)

companies.name: Pyrocell
companies.what: Setra-Preem joint venture converting sawmill sawdust to pyrolysis oil at Gavle for co-processing at Preem's Lysekil refinery
companies.signal: Producing since autumn 2021 (~25,000 t/yr design); first sawdust-to-refinery value chain in Sweden

companies.name: Twence (Empyro)
companies.what: Dutch waste-and-energy utility that owns and operates the Empyro fast-pyrolysis oil plant in Hengelo
companies.signal: Empyro running commercially since 2015 (~20 ML/yr design), acquired by Twence in 2019

companies.name: Green Fuel Nordic
companies.what: Operates the Lieksa, Finland fast-pyrolysis bio-oil plant on BTG-BL technology for industrial heating fuel
companies.signal: Commercial production since 2020; listed as commercial in IEA Bioenergy's direct-liquefaction status report

companies.name: Ensyn
companies.what: Canadian RTP fast-pyrolysis pioneer (Renfrew, Ontario plant; Envergent JV with Honeywell UOP) selling renewable fuel oil
companies.signal: Decades of commercial RFO supply, but little public activity reported since ~2023

variations.white_space: Pyrolysis oil as fuel struggles against fossil parity and depends on a handful of refinery co-processing partners, which is why the plant fleet has barely grown since 2015; the visible opening is redirecting output to higher-value uses — carbon-removal injection feedstock (Charm's model) or specialty chemicals — rather than competing in heating fuel.

variations.name: Metallurgical and industrial biocarbon (fossil carbon substitution)
variations.description: Engineered high-purity biocarbon from wood residues replaces fossil coal and coke as reductant and energy carbon in steel, ferroalloy, silicon and battery-material production — an enormous emissions-reduction market that pulls pyrolysis to true heavy-industrial scale.

companies.name: Aymium
companies.what: Minnesota producer of patented high-purity biocarbon pellets qualified as coal/coke replacement in metals, silicon and energy; operates a Michigan facility
companies.signal: $150M raise (Feb 2025, Bedrock Industries); Weyerhaeuser MOU targeting 1.5 Mt/yr via TerraForge JV, first ~$100M plant in McComb, Mississippi

companies.name: Vow Green Metals (Arbion Industries)
companies.what: Norwegian VOW spinoff building the Honefoss biocarbon plant (wood waste to ~10-30 kt/yr) for ferroalloy smelters, with bio-oil co-product
companies.signal: €26.2M EU Innovation Fund grant for large-scale project; HitecVision-backed; rebranded Arbion Industries

companies.name: Aperam BioEnergia
companies.what: Stainless-steel group Aperam's Brazilian eucalyptus charcoal operation, decades-scale supplier to its own 'green steel' mills and now a Puro-certified biochar credit issuer
companies.signal: ~10,000 t/yr certified biochar in 2025, tripling by 2026 — among the largest Puro.earth projects

companies.name: Weyerhaeuser
companies.what: US timber REIT entering biocarbon production and guaranteed fiber supply through the TerraForge Biocarbon Solutions JV with Aymium
companies.signal: MOU announced Dec 2025 to produce and sell 1.5 Mt/yr of biocarbon for metals

variations.white_space: Steel, ferroalloy and silicon demand for fossil-coal substitutes dwarfs current biocarbon supply, but smelter qualification cycles and securing multi-decade fiber supply are brutal for startups — openings favor forestry incumbents and licensors who control feedstock (Weyerhaeuser's entry is the tell), and a credible European/Asian counterpart to Aymium is still missing.
